b: Timothy Williamson will be the inaugural speaker in a new lecture series accompanying a new journal: The Chinese Journal of Philosophy (CJP).
Published by Oxford University Press, the CJP is an open-access (including no cost to authors) general philosophy journal.
It is edited by Roger T. Ames (Hawaii), Wei Cheng (Peking), Nicolas De Warren (Penn State), Sebastian Sunday Grève (Peking), and You Zhao (Peking).
The journal is open to submissions “from anyone working in philosophy and on all philosophical topics.” According to its website,

the journal aims to represent the multitude of topics and approaches that may fall under the heading of ‘philosophy’ in the world today, with a special focus on philosophical research that has the potential to make different traditions of thought more fruitful for one another.

That is to say, it is not a journal primarily about Chinese philosophy, anymore than the Canadian Journal of Philosophy is a journal about Canadian philosophy, or the Australasian Journal of Philosophy is about Australasian philosophy . The note, “like these other journals, the Chinese Journal of Philosophy originates in a particular region whilst editing and publishing as an international collective, operating in English, and promoting work from around the world.”
CJP is currently open for submissions and plans to begin publishing articles in April.

The launch of the journal includes the start of a new lecture series from the Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies at Peking University. Williamson’s inaugural lecture is this Wednesday, and will be delivered in person and online.
